events.title: Battle of Gettysburg Begins
events.description: Union and Confederate forces clashed near Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, beginning a three-day battle (July 1-3) that became the largest of the American Civil War in terms of casualties.
events.significance: Widely regarded as the turning point of the American Civil War; Lee's defeat ended his invasion of the North and Confederate hopes for decisive victory on Union soil.

events.title: Canadian Confederation
events.description: The British North America Act took effect, uniting the Province of Canada (split into Ontario and Quebec), Nova Scotia, and New Brunswick into the Dominion of Canada.
events.significance: Marks the founding of modern Canada, celebrated annually as Canada Day, and began its evolution toward full independence from Britain.

events.title: Battle of the Somme Begins
events.description: British and French forces launched a major offensive against German lines along the Somme River in France. The British Army suffered about 57,000 casualties on the first day, including roughly 19,000 killed, the bloodiest day in its history.
events.significance: The battle became a symbol of the horror and futility of trench warfare in World War I, lasting until November 1916 with over one million total casualties.

events.title: Chinese Communist Party Founded
events.description: The Chinese Communist Party is traditionally marked as founded in July 1921, with its first National Congress held in Shanghai beginning in late July; July 1 is officially commemorated as the Party's founding anniversary.
events.significance: The CCP went on to win the Chinese Civil War and establish the People's Republic of China in 1949, shaping modern world politics.

events.title: Hong Kong Handover
events.description: The United Kingdom transferred sovereignty of Hong Kong to the People's Republic of China, ending over 150 years of British colonial rule and establishing the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region under the 'one country, two systems' principle.
events.significance: Marked the end of one of the last major British colonial territories and a significant moment in China's emergence as a global power.
